facts.value: The aim of this course is to acquire basic subject vocabulary and to consolidate knowledge of the basic structures of the Chinese language. After this course, students should be able to conduct simple conversations in Chinese and manage typical everyday situations as well as tourist and professional/business stays in China independently.

Students should acquire linguistic and intercultural competencies as well as knowledge about China's culture and society, which are beneficial for activities in the area of Chinese-German economic relations and for establishing and maintaining contacts with Chinese partners.
Reading comprehension and writing skills are tested in a 90-minute exam during the last week of lectures. A graded certificate will be issued for successfully passing the exam.
Unit 1 – Chinese pronunciation, Unit 2 – Greetings, introducing oneself, Unit 3 – Exchanging simple information, Unit 4 – About the family, Unit 5 – About various things
Details about the textbook will be provided in the first class.

The economic-related language competencies will be gradually built up. The focus remains on oral communication skills, enabling simple conversations on topics of Chinese-German economic cooperation and foreign trade.
Students should acquire basic knowledge of the Chinese character script, including how to use character-based text programs.
The language competence will be tested at the end of the course in a 90-minute exam during the last week of lectures.
Unit 1 – Formal introduction and greeting, Unit 2 – Description of people, Unit 3 – Daily work life, Unit 4 – Problems at work
Chinese Experience - Official Communication in China.
